title: bug: caller-supplied candidate and check-run ids that differ only by case overwrite each other on a case-insensitive filesystem
description:
Found by QA of the Wave 1 integration gate (task-808869c5). Code refs are at HEAD 09513e0.

`moe.record_candidate` and `moe.record_check_run` accept an optional caller-supplied `id` (state/candidateStore.ts:224 `input.id ?? generateId('cand')`; checkRunStore.ts:277-279). util/sanitize.ts:106 allows mixed case. The in-memory maps are case-sensitive, but each record is persisted as `<id>.json` (state/persistence.ts:331).

On NTFS or a default APFS volume:
1. record_candidate {id: 'Cand-1', ...} is recorded.
2. record_candidate {id: 'cand-1', ...} with a different treeSha misses the `state.candidates.get(id)` lookup (candidateStore.ts:225-226), so it is not refused CANDIDATE_IMMUTABLE.
3. Its atomic rename overwrites Cand-1.json. After a reload only 'cand-1' exists, and every check run, review or receipt bound to 'Cand-1' dangles.

The same applies to check runs. The wrappers generate lowercase uuid ids, so only agent-supplied or third-party ids can collide. That is why this is LOW. It is still an immutability bypass on the daemon's primary platform.
definitionOfDone: record_candidate and record_check_run refuse an id that equals an existing record's id case-insensitively, or normalize ids to one case, and the rule is documented in docs/SCHEMA.md
A test per store fails on the old behaviour (a case-variant id is recorded as a new record)

implementationPlan.note:
RED written before any guard. Prerequisite task-31fe6dc8 is DONE (completion 862a99f is on moe/work-2026-09-13). I found the code by symbol name.
- candidateStore.test.ts: new it 'refuses an id that differs from a stored candidate only by case', placed after the replay test. It records Cand-1, then cand-1 twice: first with a DIFFERENT treeSha, then with identical content. Both must be refused with one exact toEqual on {code -32002, codeName CANDIDATE_ID_CASE_COLLISION, the full '[CODENAME] ' message, context {candidateId:'Cand-1', requestedId:'cand-1'}}. Afterwards: candidates.size 1, getCandidate('Cand-1') still equals the first record, its bytes are unchanged, and the dir lists exactly ['Cand-1.json'].
- checkRunStore.test.ts: the same shape with Check-1/check-1, CHECK_RUN_ID_CASE_COLLISION and context {checkRunId, requestedId}. The candidate binding stays valid (cand-a/treeA), so the refusal is the id rule and not a tree mismatch. It uses snapshot() for the bytes and the map, plus size 1 and checkFiles ['Check-1.json'].
- The existing same-id immutability and replay tests are untouched.

RED on today's code (`env -u MOE_PROJECT_PATH -u MOE_WORKER_ID npx vitest run src/state/candidateStore.test.ts src/state/checkRunStore.test.ts -t "only by case"`):
  FAIL candidateStore > refuses an id that differs from a stored candidate only by case: Error: expected a MoeError refusal, but the call succeeded (candidateStore.test.ts:207)
  FAIL checkRunStore > refuses an id that differs from a stored check run only by case: Error: expected a MoeError refusal, but the call succeeded (checkRunStore.test.ts:332)
  Tests 2 failed | 125 skipped (127)
Both fail because the case-variant id is RECORDED as a second record.

Real-NTFS probe of the unfixed store, from a scratch tsx script outside the repo (D:/moe-scratch/dad7-probe-3c03/probe.mts, not in the suite): {"outcome":"RECORDED duplicate=false","mapKeys":["Cand-1","cand-1"],"files":["cand-1.json"],"firstBytesUnchanged":false}, and after reload only ["cand-1:tree d4d4"]. The rename replaced Cand-1.json and even took the new name, and the reload lost Cand-1 entirely.

Edits were made with the built-in Edit tool on purpose. All 8 target files are LF, and Serena replace_content rewrites a file to CRLF and is missing from the wrappers' TOOL harvest (mem:gotcha-contested-path-needs-edit-tool-to-land). docs/SCHEMA.md and docs/MCP_SERVER.md are peer-declared (task-16aac8b4, task-d5b7e6a2).

implementationPlan.description:
THE SHARED CHECK plus the candidate guard, in state/candidateStore.ts. It is the home the sibling stores already import from (checkRunStore, receiptStore and reviewStore all import it, and it imports none of them, so no cycle: stateModules.test.ts fails on a runtime cycle inside src/state).

1. New export:
     export function caseVariantId(ids: Iterable<string>, id: string): string | undefined
   It returns the first stored id that is NOT equal to `id` but equals it after toLowerCase(), else undefined.
   Its doc comment must carry the why: every record is persisted as <id>.json, NTFS and a default APFS volume treat 'Cand-1.json' and 'cand-1.json' as ONE file, the in-memory map is case-sensitive, so the same-id immutability check never sees the collision and the second write silently overwrites the first. After a reload only one record exists and every check run, review or receipt bound to the other one dangles.
   Note in the comment that it is a linear scan and why that is fine: a record is written about once per landing, so the scan is nothing next to the write it guards.
2. In recordCandidate, right after the exact-match branch ('const stored = state.candidates.get(id); if (stored) return ...'), add: if caseVariantId(state.candidates.keys(), id) returns an existing id, throw a MoeError(MoeErrorCode.STATE_CONFLICT, ..., { candidateId: <existing>, requestedId: <id> }, 'CANDIDATE_ID_CASE_COLLISION').
   Message: `Candidate id <id> differs only by case from the existing candidate <existing>; each record is one file (<id>.json), and NTFS and a default APFS volume treat those two names as the same file, so recording this one would overwrite the other. Supply a distinct id - a stored id keeps the case it was given, and references match it exactly.`
3. Order matters: the exact-id replay stays FIRST, so an idempotent retry after a crash is untouched, and the collision check runs before assertAttemptOfTask and before any write.
4. Error handling: the new check only reads the in-memory map and throws the same MoeError shape as its neighbours, so every refusal still writes no file and publishes no event, and a caller sees one -32002 with a codeName it can branch on. The helper itself cannot throw.
5. Add 'caseVariantId' to the export allowlist in state/candidateStore.test.ts, which task-31fe6dc8 also edits.
6. Run the candidate test: it is GREEN now.

CHECK-RUN GUARD in state/checkRunStore.ts. Import caseVariantId from './candidateStore.js' (it already imports getCandidate from there) and apply it in recordCheckRun right after its exact-match branch, before the write.

Throw MoeError(MoeErrorCode.STATE_CONFLICT, ..., { checkRunId: <existing>, requestedId: <id> }, 'CHECK_RUN_ID_CASE_COLLISION'), with the same message shape as the candidate one, reading 'Check run id ...' and 'the existing check run ...'.

Keep the existing order: validate, assertTreeOfCandidate, exact-id replay or refusal, then this check. So a caller with a bad tree still gets CHECK_RUN_TREE_MISMATCH, and an exact-id retry still replays. Error handling matches the candidate store exactly: refuse before the write, one -32002, nothing persisted.

Run the check-run test: GREEN.

SIBLING HARDENING, reviewStore. Deliberately beyond the DoD's two stores, and called out here so a reviewer can weigh it: recordReview has the identical shape (optional caller-supplied id, exact-match map lookup, one <id>.json per record), so the same overwrite exists there. It is unreachable today, because qa_approve and qa_reject never pass an id, which is why it is hardening and not a second bug. Leaving the third sibling different is how this slice keeps drifting (see the copies task-31fe6dc8 had to re-align).

1. state/reviewStore.ts: import caseVariantId and apply it in recordReview right after its exact-match branch, throwing MoeError(MoeErrorCode.STATE_CONFLICT, ..., { reviewId: <existing>, requestedId: <id> }, 'REVIEW_ID_CASE_COLLISION') with the same message shape and the same refuse-before-write ordering.
2. tools/qaApprove.test.ts already drives recordReview directly (the REVIEW_IMMUTABLE tests use ids like 'review-x'). Add one it() there in the same style: a stored 'Review-1', then 'review-1' with a different summary, refused with REVIEW_ID_CASE_COLLISION, and state.reviews.size still 1.
3. If a reviewer would rather keep this task to its DoD, this step can be dropped whole: nothing in the other steps depends on it.

DOCS.
1. docs/SCHEMA.md, in the Candidate, CheckRun and Review sections:
   - In each interface block, extend the `id` comment: a caller-supplied id must match [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128} AND must not differ from an existing record's id only by case.
   - In each Immutability or Append-only paragraph, add one sentence: ids are compared case-insensitively for EXISTENCE, because a record is one file, <id>.json, and NTFS and a default APFS volume treat 'Cand-1.json' and 'cand-1.json' as the same file. A colliding id is refused (CANDIDATE_ID_CASE_COLLISION, CHECK_RUN_ID_CASE_COLLISION, REVIEW_ID_CASE_COLLISION), a stored id keeps the case it was given, and reference fields such as candidateId are matched exactly.
   - Say plainly what is NOT covered: records that already collided before this rule (two files written on a case-sensitive filesystem) are left alone, and an operator resolves those by hand.
2. docs/MCP_SERVER.md: add the refusal to the error list of moe.record_candidate and moe.record_check_run, in their existing style:
   `-32002 CANDIDATE_ID_CASE_COLLISION`: the supplied id differs only by case from an existing candidate's id; supply a distinct id.
   `-32002 CHECK_RUN_ID_CASE_COLLISION`: the same for a check run.
   Also extend each tool's 'Immutable' note with one clause, so the rule is where a reader of the tool contract meets it. No review tool takes an id, so nothing is added there.

VERIFY.
1. cd packages/moe-daemon && npx tsc --noEmit: prints nothing.
2. cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test: green. A file that flakes under fleet load is rerun alone and reported (mem:moes-test-env-quirks).
3. Prove the guard is in all three stores and nowhere else: grep -rn 'caseVariantId' packages/moe-daemon/src --include=*.ts. Expect the definition plus one call in each of candidateStore, checkRunStore and reviewStore. Paste it.
4. Prove the file-level effect on this box, which is NTFS, so it is the real platform: in a scratch project, record 'Cand-1' then 'cand-1' through the store and confirm .moe/candidates has exactly one file and the first record's bytes are unchanged. A two-line node script against a ToolTestHarness-style temp dir is enough; do not add it to the suite.
5. For complete_task, verification is 'cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test' with its tail as outputTail.

SELF-REVIEW, posted as a task comment:
1. Does an exact-id retry still replay byte-identically, and does a differing exact-id record still get CANDIDATE_IMMUTABLE, CHECK_RUN_IMMUTABLE or REVIEW_IMMUTABLE? The new check must run AFTER that branch.
2. Does any refusal write a file or publish an event? All three refuse before the write.
3. Do reference lookups still match exactly? A check run naming 'cand-1' when the candidate is 'Cand-1' still gets CANDIDATE_NOT_FOUND, which is the honest answer; explain why normalizing ids instead would have forced every reference field to normalize too.
4. The scan is over the whole store map. Say what n is in practice and why it is irrelevant here.
5. What about records that ALREADY collide from a case-sensitive filesystem? Named as out of scope in docs/SCHEMA.md; confirm the wording is there.
6. Do the wrappers still work unchanged? They generate lowercase cand-<uuid> and check-<uuid> ids, so no live seat can hit this refusal; confirm nothing in scripts/ needs a change.
7. git diff --stat: only the 8 planned files.

reopenReason: Human approved promotion: QA-filed case-collision bug on candidate/check-run ids, code refs included, architects idle.
planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 8 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Normalize ids to lower case (the DoD's other option): rejected. The record's id would stop matching what the caller sent, and every reference field would have to normalize too (record_check_run's candidateId, the receipt and review bindings, the projection lookups), or a caller that recorded 'Cand-1' would get CANDIDATE_NOT_FOUND for its own candidate. It also breaks the wrapper's echo check, which compares every sent field against the stored record.
- Guard inside state.writeEntity, so every collection is covered at once: rejected. Tasks are rewritten constantly through the same path, so a per-write directory scan would cost on the hot path, and writeEntity cannot tell a legitimate rewrite of the same id from a new colliding one without the store's map.
- Reuse CANDIDATE_IMMUTABLE for the collision: rejected. Its context carries differingFields, which means nothing here, and the fix a caller must apply is different: pick another id, not record under a new one.
- Skip reviewStore: considered, and rejected in step 4, which is written so a reviewer can drop it if they disagree.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Three stores share the shape: an optional caller-supplied id, an exact-match map lookup for immutability, and one <id>.json per record written through state.writeEntity. Only record_candidate and record_check_run expose the id over MCP; qa_approve and qa_reject never pass a review id.
- candidateStore is the import hub of the slice: checkRunStore, receiptStore, reviewStore, deliveryProjection and delivery/policy all import it, and it imports none of them. task-31fe6dc8 is already making it the home of the shared shape checks, so caseVariantId belongs there too.
- candidateStore.test.ts pins the store's exported symbols, so a new export must be added to that allowlist.
- Review-store behaviour is tested from tools/qaApprove.test.ts, which drives recordReview directly with ids like 'review-x'.
- The existing refusals in these stores are STATE_CONFLICT (-32002) with a per-record codeName, which is the shape the new refusals copy.
planningNotes.risks:
- Serialization: dependsOn task-31fe6dc8, which edits all three stores and candidateStore.test.ts. Start after it lands and re-locate code by symbol name.
- Keep the exact-id replay first, or an idempotent retry after a crash starts being refused, which would break the receipt and gate paths.
- Do not weaken the existing immutability tests.
- Watch the allowlist test: a new export fails it until the list is updated, and that is also this task's second red signal.
- Pre-existing colliding files (written on a case-sensitive filesystem, then opened on Windows) are NOT repaired by this change; document it rather than writing a migration.
- No wrapper change: both wrappers generate lowercase uuid ids, so no live seat can hit these refusals. Confirm in the self-review.
